examples.question_text: An account contains $\$0$ before the first payment. A deposit of $\$a$ is made at the beginning of each year for $n$ years. Interest at rate $r$ per annum compounds annually. Derive the future value at the end of year $n$, for $r\ne0$.
examples.solution_text:
The first deposit earns $n$ years of interest and the final deposit earns one year.
$FV=a(1+r)^n+a(1+r)^{n-1}+\cdots+a(1+r)$.
In increasing-power order, the series has first term $a(1+r)$, common ratio $1+r$ and $n$ terms.
$\begin{aligned} FV&=a(1+r)\left[1+(1+r)+\cdots+(1+r)^{n-1}\right]\\&=a(1+r)\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{(1+r)-1}\\&=a(1+r)\frac{(1+r)^n-1}{r}.\end{aligned}$
If $r=0$, the deposits earn no interest and $FV=na$.

examples.question_text:
A saver deposits $\$2400$ on 1 January each year for seven years into an initially empty account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
(a) Derive a geometric-series expression and calculate the balance at the end of the seventh year, to the nearest cent.
(b) Calculate the value of the first deposit at that date, to the nearest dollar.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The seven deposits earn seven, six, …, one years of interest.
$FV=2400(1.06)^7+2400(1.06)^6+\cdots+2400(1.06)$.
In increasing-power order, the first term is $2400(1.06)$, the common ratio is $1.06$ and there are seven terms.
$\begin{aligned} FV&=2400(1.06)\left[1+1.06+\cdots+1.06^6\right]\\&=\frac{2400(1.06)(1.06^7-1)}{1.06-1}\\&\approx\$21\,353.92.\end{aligned}$
(b) The first deposit earns seven full years of interest.
$\begin{aligned} V&=2400(1.06)^7\\&\approx\$3609\quad\text{(nearest dollar)}.\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Priya deposits $\$320$ at the beginning of each month for three years into an initially empty account earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Derive a geometric-series expression and calculate the balance at the end of the three years, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
The monthly interest rate is $r=0.06/12=0.005$, and there are $n=3\times12=36$ deposits.
The first deposit earns 36 months of interest and the final deposit earns one month.
$FV=320(1.005)^{36}+320(1.005)^{35}+\cdots+320(1.005)$.
In increasing-power order, the first term is $320(1.005)$, the common ratio is $1.005$ and there are 36 terms.
$\begin{aligned} FV&=320(1.005)\left[1+1.005+\cdots+1.005^{35}\right]\\&=\frac{320(1.005)(1.005^{36}-1)}{0.005}\\&\approx\$12\,650.49.\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A club wants $\$30\,000$ at the end of five years. It will make equal deposits at the beginning of each month into an initially empty account earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Derive a geometric-series equation and find the required monthly deposit, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Let the monthly deposit be $M$. The monthly rate is $r=0.072/12=0.006$, and there are $n=5\times12=60$ deposits.
The first deposit earns 60 months of interest and the final deposit earns one month.
$30000=M(1.006)^{60}+M(1.006)^{59}+\cdots+M(1.006)$.
In increasing-power order, the first term is $M(1.006)$, the common ratio is $1.006$ and there are 60 terms.
$\begin{aligned} 30000&=M(1.006)\left[1+1.006+\cdots+1.006^{59}\right]\\30000&=\frac{M(1.006)(1.006^{60}-1)}{0.006}\\M&=\frac{30000(0.006)}{1.006(1.006^{60}-1)}\\M&\approx\$414.38.\end{aligned}$
Keep the accumulation factor unrounded. Rounding the deposit to cents can make the final balance slightly different from the exact target.

examples.derivation: The n deposits earn n through one interest periods. Reordering gives first term a(1+r), ratio 1+r and n terms, so FV=a(1+r)((1+r)^n-1)/r for r≠0. For r=0, FV=na.
Summing 2400(1.06)^k for k=1,…,7 gives 21353.92298123369, rounding to $21,353.92. The first deposit grows to 2400(1.06)^7=3608.7126215792655, rounding to $3609.
The monthly rate is 0.005 and there are 36 deposits. Summing 320(1.005)^k for k=1,…,36 gives 12650.491356642031, rounding to $12,650.49.
The monthly rate is 0.006 and there are 60 deposits. From 30000=M·1.006(1.006^60−1)/0.006, M=414.38453735790324, rounding to $414.38. The stated rounding qualification is correct.
